text:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Canary v10 (encoder-quant, us-west) p99 latency spike detected — streaming stalls observed. Current affected routes: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate. p95 ~ 220ms -> 480ms, p99 ~ 1.6s -> 4.8s. triggering paging to #incidents. metrics: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/3333337777 :rotating_light:
eng-oncall: I’m on it. paging SRE. can anyone grab initial blast radius?
maria: oncall here — seeing errors and repeated client reconnects for the payments funnel (orders-service). customers seeing timeouts around 3-5s.
sre-til: I’m paged, joining. can we confirm only canary traffic? what % rolled?
leo: rollout was at 10% for canary v10, traffic shift started ~3333337500. router logs show weighted routing to v10 across us-west only.
maria: confirmed: only canary pool A in us-west-2 has v10. other regions healthy.
jen: adding quick checks — looking at encoder kv metrics, tail KV latency is elevated and mem pressure on pods with model shard 3.
eng-oncall: copying logs ->
```
[2026-03-15T03:01:12Z] pod/canary-v10-3 kernel stall, kv-lookup latency 120ms -> 520ms
[2026-03-15T03:01:12Z] stream-session id=abcd reconnect due to wait > 2s
```
sam: any immediate mitigation? can we pull traffic back to v9? :point_up:
maria: agreed. customer impact = payment timeouts; priority: rollback or shift traffic off canary.
leo: we should try a soft-rollback: change weight for v10 -> 0 and route 100% to v9. do we have a quick command?
eng-oncall: runbook step 4: update-routing.sh takes model and weight args. I’ll run now.
eng-oncall: `/opt/bin/update-routing.sh --model canary-v10 --weight 0 --reason "p99 tail regress"`
Incident Bot: deploy-bot: routing update requested by eng-oncall. diff: v10: 10% -> 0%, v9: 90% -> 100%.
eng-oncall: executed. waiting for propagation (~30s).
jen: metrics after 45s: p99 trending down to 1.2s, p95 back to ~250ms. reconnects dropping.
sre-til: good. start restoring traffic telemetry for orders-service. maria can you verify customer-side errors?
maria: error rates on orders-service 5xx dropped from 6.4% -> 0.8% after shift. confirming majority of complaints were us-west.
sam: thumbs. we should also capture heap/kv evictions and snapshot logs for postmortem. jen can you pull pod gc and eviction events for the last 10m?
jen: pulling now, attaching snippet shortly.
jen: attached: `evictions.log` shows repeated KV cache evictions on shard-3 at 03:00:48Z and 03:01:05Z. likely eviction thrash under quantized encoder.
leo: hypothesis: v10 quantization profile mis-tunes KV prefetch leading to thrash under steady streaming workloads -> tail latency.
eng-oncall: create incident ticket and hand off to rollout owners. I’ll open INC-2026-3318.
eng-oncall: INC-2026-3318 created: Canary v10 induced tail latency -> rollback executed.
Incident Bot: paging summary: paged 3 oncall, 2 SREs, notify #customer-impact.
maria: queued message to CS: "We observed elevated latency impacting streaming calls for a canary model in us-west. Root cause under investigation; we rolled back the canary and are monitoring. If you see persistent errors, please DM support."
support-bot: customer ticket #C-81234 linked to incident INC-2026-3318. Notified affected accounts: orders-prod, checkout-api-prod.
sre-til: next steps: collect heap snapshots, model profiler traces, and kv-cache histograms from v10 pods. schedule a deeper postmortem.
leo: assign to eng-runtime (me) + research (jen) + infra (sre-til). target postmortem draft EOD.
maria: also recommend temporary gating in rollout pipeline: require shadowing validation for 1h with latency SLAs before >5% shift.
eng-oncall: handoff to daytime oncall @leo and @maria at 08:00 PST for follow-up.
sam: adding retro action for compiling quantization test harness for streaming workloads.
eng-oncall: closing paging loop — live mitigation successful, customer impact reduced. keep thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
